slot.brief: Statements on solubility and thermal decomposition of group 2 sulphates/carbonates; identify correct ones.

stem: Consider the following statements: I. Solubility of group 2 carbonates decreases down the group. II. Thermal stability of group 2 carbonates increases down the group. III. Solubility of group 2 sulphates increases down the group. IV. Gypsum heated at about 373 K gives plaster of Paris. Which statements are correct?

verdicts.working: I and II are correct: carbonate solubility decreases and thermal stability increases down Group 2. III is false; sulphate solubility decreases down the group. IV is correct: heating gypsum near 373 K gives plaster of Paris.

working:
Group 2 carbonate solubility decreases down the group; thermal stability increases down the group. Sulphate solubility decreases down the group, so III is wrong. Gypsum on heating at about 373 K forms plaster of Paris. Correct: I, II and IV.

Independent check: I and II are correct: carbonate solubility decreases and thermal stability increases down Group 2. III is false; sulphate solubility decreases down the group. IV is correct: heating gypsum near 373 K gives plaster of Paris.
solution:
Group 2 carbonate solubility decreases, while their thermal stability increases down the group. Sulphate solubility also decreases down the group, so III is false.
Heating gypsum at about $373\,\text{K}$ forms plaster of Paris; hence I, II and IV are correct.
